If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want an angular plate with two quadratic plates positioned in right angel to each other. The edge length of the plates is 140mm. They are 10mm thick. On one of the two plates I would like to have a quadratic cutout, 45x45mm, centred on the plate. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step by step (no execution yet)

1. Establish a global coordinate system  
   • X-axis: long edge of both plates (140 mm)  
   • Y-axis: width of the horizontal plate (140 mm) and the 10 mm thickness of the vertical plate  
   • Z-axis: 10 mm thickness of the horizontal plate and 140 mm height of the vertical plate  
   The origin (0,0,0) is chosen at the common bottom-rear corner where both plates meet.

2. Add the horizontal plate (plate 1)  
   • Base-point: (x=0, y=0, z=0)  
   • Size: x_size = 140 mm, y_size = 140 mm, z_size = 10 mm  
   • subtraction = False (it builds the initial solid)

3. Add the vertical plate (plate 2) perpendicular to the first one  
   • Base-point: (x=0, y=0, z=0) — shares the origin with plate 1 so both plates intersect in the 10 mm-thick edge zone (0 ≤ y ≤ 10, 0 ≤ z ≤ 10)  
   • Size: x_size = 140 mm, y_size = 10 mm (its thickness), z_size = 140 mm (its height)  
   • subtraction = False

4. Prepare the centred square cut-out (45 mm × 45 mm) in the middle of the horizontal plate only  
   • Plate 1 spans 0 ≤ x,y ≤ 140 mm.  
   • The cut-out edges run from 47.5 mm to 92.5 mm in both X and Y ( (140 – 45)/2 = 47.5 ).  
   • Base-point of the cut-out block: (x = 47.5, y = 47.5, z = 0).  
   • Size: x_size = 45 mm, y_size = 45 mm, z_size = 10 mm – cuts through the full thickness of plate 1 only.  
   • subtraction = True

5. Populate the arrays for a single functions.block(...) call containing all three rectangular prisms  
   x_size = [140, 140, 45]  
   y_size = [140,  10, 45]  
   z_size = [ 10, 140, 10]  
   x       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   y       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   z       = [  0,   0, 0]  
   subtraction = [False, False, True]

6. Issue the block call with those arrays to create the two plates and subtract the cut-out in one step.

7. (Optional but recommended) Follow with a functions.finished(allFunctionsCalled = True) call to mark completion.

When you are ready for the actual function calls, just let me know and I will prepare them exactly as described above.
